floor.title: The index of an ego network is set by how many links it has
floor.caption: Every shape of ego network whose index is known exactly, in all the worlds read, their twins and the four networks with no history: a dot for each pair of links and index that occurs (up to 40 links). The grey steps are l(m), the shortest addition chain of the number of links: no shape can be built in fewer joins, since each join at most adds two sizes already made. The dashed line is m − 1, a link at a time, the most any shape needs. Blue: shapes whose index is exactly l(m), the floor; orange: shapes above it. Of 16,577 shapes counted (a shape found in two networks counts twice), 1,657 lie above the floor; they are the ego networks of 12,040 of 999,082 agents.
floor.recipe:
**Runs.** The thirty worlds of B1 at 100,000 tokens (Experiment 10, `B1-100000-s001` … `-s030`) after the game of iteration 1,499; the ten worlds of B2 at 10,000 tokens (Experiment 16, `B2-10000-s001` … `-s010`) after the game of iteration 1,999; and seven worlds of round 3 of the screen, 30,000 tokens each, after the game of iteration 2,999: the five healthiest by the product (`B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`, `B1-30000-8526cf-s4006` played strongest first, `B1-30000-af1e28-s3018`, `B1-30000-625bc7-s3080`, `B1-30000-38aee9-s3057`), the densest (`B1-30000-4ac946-s3094`) and the star (`B1-30000-511930-s3020`); and four networks built from seed 23 with no history (see the figure of the worlds).

**Data.** From each run's last frame, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `book_data.frame_at(run, t, 2)` (the agents and their connections after the game); the shapes are kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.assembly.json`.

1. For every agent, its ego network: its links to its neighbours, and the links among those neighbours (`book_assembly.ego_links`).
2. Sort the ego networks into shapes, one for each class of isomorphic graphs (`book_assembly.Shapes`: a canonical form, as nauty makes one, with twins skipped; above 16 links a Weisfeiler–Lehman hash first). A shape's copy number is how many agents have it.
3. Each shape's assembly index (`book_assembly.Assembler`): the fewest joins that build it from single links, reusing anything built, found by a search from the shape down, deepening from the addition-chain bound l(m) of its m links. Exact for every shape of at most 16 links; for a larger shape that two or more agents share, exact when the search ends within 20,000 units of work, and otherwise an interval; for a larger star, l(d).
4. The twin: the same agents with as many links each, wired at random (`book_graph.degree_preserving`, seed 23), read the same way.
5. Mark each pair (links, index) that some shape with an exact index has: blue if the index is l(links), orange if it is more.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py assembly`.

copies.title: Copies fall with the index, in the worlds as in their twins
copies.caption: Assembly theory's own picture: one dot for every shape of ego network, at its assembly index (across) and its copy number, the agents whose ego network has that shape (up, on a logarithmic scale). Orange: the network's shapes, a world's or the random space's; blue: its random twin's, the same agents with as many links each, wired at random. The dots are spread a little sideways at random so that they do not hide each other; only shapes whose index is known exactly are drawn. Assembly theory reads many copies of a shape of high index as the mark of selection; a shape with one copy adds nothing to the assembly A.

worlds.title: The assembly of a world is about that of its twin
worlds.caption: The assembly A = Σ e^{a_i} (n_i − 1) / N_T of each network's ego networks, a_i the index of shape i, n_i its copies and N_T the agents with at least one link. Orange: the network; blue: its random twin. A dot per world; the bars are the medians. B1: the thirty worlds at 100,000 tokens; B2: the ten at 10,000; round 3: its five healthiest worlds; dense: its densest world, s3094; star: its world held together by one hub. The last four are built with no history, from seed 23. Triangles: a triangular lattice on a torus, 10,000 nodes; cubes: a cubic lattice on a three-dimensional torus, 10,648 nodes; tree: a random tree of 10,000 nodes; space: a random space, 10,000 points in a cube that wraps round, joined when close enough for 4 links each on average. Where a shared shape's index is only bounded, A is drawn at its lower bound.

round3.title: Every world of round 3 holds about as much assembly as its twin, however healthy
round3.caption: One dot for each of the 82 worlds of round 3 that lived to the end of their 3,000 iterations, read after the game of iteration 2,999. Orange: Experiment 40, every setting drawn at random and every token staked at once; blue and green: the eight draws of Experiments 41 and 42, staking a token at a time, the weakest stakes placed first or the strongest. Left: the assembly A of a world's ego networks (up) against its random twin's (across), both on logarithmic axes; on the dashed line a world holds exactly as much as its twin. Right: the world's A over its twin's against its health, the product of its six criteria's scores (Which worlds are healthy?); on the dashed line the two are equal. Where a shared shape's index is only bounded, A is taken at its lower bound.
round3.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen that lived to the end: 70 of Experiment 40's 84 and 12 of the 16 of Experiments 41 and 42 (30,000 tokens, 3,000 iterations), after the game of iteration 2,999

**Data.** From each run's last frame, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `book_data.frame_at(run, t, 2)` (the agents and their connections after the game); the shapes are kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.assembly.json`; each world's health from `research/screen/health.json` (`health.product`).

1. For every agent, its ego network: its links to its neighbours, and the links among those neighbours (`book_assembly.ego_links`).
2. Sort the ego networks into shapes, one for each class of isomorphic graphs (`book_assembly.Shapes`: a canonical form, as nauty makes one, with twins skipped; above 16 links a Weisfeiler–Lehman hash first). A shape's copy number is how many agents have it.

5. A = Σ e^{a_i} (n_i − 1) / N_T over the shapes, for the world and for its twin.
6. Left: the world's A against its twin's. Right: their ratio against the world's health.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py assembly`.

life.title: Through a world's life, its assembly follows its twin's
life.caption: The assembly A of the ego networks after the game of every 100th iteration of a B1 world (top) and every 250th of round 3's healthiest world (bottom), from the founders' ring at iteration 0 to the end. brains.title: A genotype's path in the family tree is a clock
brains.caption: The depth of a genotype: how many changes its line has had since its founder, the length of the only pathway the family tree records. Solid: the median over the living agents' genotypes; dotted: the deepest. B1 offers every brain a change after every game and every newborn's brain one at birth, each taken with probability 0.2; B2 offers one only when a brain is copied, to a newborn or to a node won; round 3's world s3042 mixes a newborn's brain from two parents, of which the tree keeps one, and 1,846,124 of its genotypes have a parent that never appears in a frame, so its tree is cut into short pieces and its depths say little. The grey dashed line is 0.2 changes an iteration.
brains.recipe:
**Runs.** `B1-100000-s001`, `B2-10000-s001` and `B1-30000-b82ad0-s3042`.

**Data.** From every frame of each run, in order (`brain_ids`, `parent_brain_ids`); kept in `GraphOfLifeRuns/.book/<run>.genotype-depth.json`.

1. Give each genotype, the first time it is seen, the depth of its parent plus one (a founder's: 0; a parent never seen counts as a founder).
2. After the games of every 100th iteration (250th in round 3) and the last, the median and the largest depth of the genotypes the living carry.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py assembly`.
